以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
A refrigerator crisper drawer can look like a simple box. But its humidity control offers two ways to slow how fresh food can go bad.

Many refrigerators have a low-humidity setting and a high-humidity setting. The low-humidity drawer lets more air move through it. That matters for foods that release ethylene gas, a natural gas produced as some fruit matures.

Apples, pears, bananas, and tomatoes release a lot of ethylene. If nearby produce is exposed to the gas for too long, it may ripen too quickly and spoil. In a more ventilated drawer, some of that gas can escape.

The high-humidity setting is more enclosed. It helps keep moisture around foods that can lose water quickly. Leafy greens, such as kale, and vegetables such as broccoli can wilt when they dry out.

So the main rule is not simply “fruit goes here, vegetables go there.” The better question is what the food is likely to do in storage. Will it release gas that affects nearby food? Or will it lose water and wilt? That is the real job of the two settings.

【Point One】
The humidity control is not just a general “freshness” button. It is a choice between ventilation and moisture.

When food is not keeping well, ask what kind of problem you are seeing. Is it losing water and becoming limp? Or is it causing nearby produce to ripen too quickly? That question gives you a more useful guide than the food’s name alone. It also explains why the two drawers should not be treated as interchangeable containers.

【Point Two】
There is one more question: does the food belong in the refrigerator at all?

Strawberries and citrus fruits, including oranges, favor high humidity. Their best humidity range is about 90 to 95 percent. Tomatoes and bananas, however, are recommended for counter storage. Potatoes, sweet potatoes, onions, and garlic do not need refrigeration and are better kept in a cool, dry place.
